(Tesla vehicles generally (fleet-wide aggregate of miles driven with FSD Supervised engaged compared with miles driven without it), implicitly over the period the vendor reports.) vs A regulatory hazard judgment that specific FSD Beta behaviors (exceeding speed limits, proceeding through intersections unlawfully or unpredictably) elevate crash risk relative to lawful driving behavior. (Particular defective behaviors of a particular FSD Beta software version in particular driving situations (intersections, speed-limit zones), not aggregate crash outcomes across FSD-engaged driving.)

0.42 — Collision reduction vs safeguard evaluation: Vehicles with FSD engaged have fewer collisions

A comparative safety outcome: the collision rate (per mile or per vehicle) is lower when Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is engaged than when the same vehicles are driven without it. (Tesla vehicles in the field, comparing two driving conditions (FSD engaged vs. not engaged), presented as a fleet-wide/aggregate rate with no stated time window.) vs An absolute tally of adverse events: hundreds of crashes and some deaths reported in incidents associated with Tesla's driver-assistance systems (Autopilot and FSD combined), as counted in regulatory incident reporting. (Reported crash incidents involving Tesla Autopilot and FSD lumped together, over the reporting period covered; no non-engaged comparison group, no exposure denominator (miles driven), and no separation of FSD from Autopilot.)

A functional capability claim: that FSD (Supervised) is able to perform the routine daily drive, including the most common and error-prone driving tasks. (Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) feature as offered to customers, in ordinary everyday driving conditions, current product generation.) vs An evaluative judgment about the accuracy of the product's name — that the marketing label 'Full Self-Driving Capability' overstates what the system is, i.e., it is not fully autonomous. It is a headline conclusion, not a measurement of which driving tasks the system can or cannot handle. (Tesla's FSD offering in general (naming/marketing), at the time of the source's publication; no specified set of driving tasks, conditions, or performance data.)
